note: Decisions the protocol screen has already been given, with their reasons. A row an existing ruling covers is reported under it rather than in ACT — answered, not hidden. Scope rulings expire on purpose: see scripts/lib/rulings.mjs. Edited by hand or by the Monday run; every entry needs a reason a stranger could re-examine.

rulings.reason: The nonstandard-scheme advisory was narrowed to the spec's own four families and spec-scheme-not-exact added. Shipped 2026-09-14 with red witnessed first.
The eleven MPP classes now cite draft-httpauth-payment-01 at a real read date, with the renewal diff recorded. Shipped 2026-09-14.

We do not settle on Tempo. Its TIPs are read so that the day a named counterparty asks for it we are not starting from zero, and for the settlement mechanics MPP's charge methods cite — but a TIP moving is never work on shipped code here.

Answered 2026-09-14: `ready` does mean the same thing — the verdict-moving checks read the scheme-independent envelope §4 requires of every scheme, and no verdict is wrong on a non-exact door. What ready did not cover was §6.1's extra.paymentFlow, where upfront and escrow spend the buyer before the handler runs; our own client already dropped those entries and the free preflight said nothing. Advisory settles-before-delivery shipped. Record: docs/SCHEME_VERDICT_DEPTH_2026-09.md.
Five of the seven extensions x402 publishes have no reader here, including extension-offer-and-receipt, which is the conformance desk's own subject.

Withdrawn as a finding: SPEC_READS.md had already recorded the move to x402-foundation, and the remaining mentions are the npm package @coinbase/x402, which is current. One later dated log entry reached for the old URL again — history, corrected by appending, never by editing.

The corpus keeps an advisory's name and not its detail, so the fragmentation time series cannot tell a real fork from our own blind spot. Retaining the scheme value changes what the corpus stores, so it is the keeper's call.
